docs.title: tinyconf
docs.text:
tinyconf is a simple and universal library for parsing configs in Go. It fills your config structs with values from drivers: default values from struct tags, YAML, JSON, TOML, INI and .properties files, environment variables, command line flags, Consul KV, HashiCorp Vault, etcd. Every driver is a separate small package, and you can add your own.

One-line ideology

The config is a plain Go struct. Where the values come from is described by struct tags and by the list of drivers, the last driver wins.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
go get github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2@latest

Minimum Go version is 1.19.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "time"

    "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2"
    "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/drivers/env"
    "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/drivers/tag"
    "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/drivers/yaml"
    "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/logger"
)

type HTTP struct {
    Host    string        `initial:"localhost" yaml:"host" env:"HTTP_HOST" doc:"http host"`
    Port    int           `initial:"8080" yaml:"port" env:"HTTP_PORT" doc:"http port"`
    Timeout time.Duration `initial:"30s" yaml:"timeout" env:"HTTP_TIMEOUT" doc:"http timeout"`
}

type Config struct {
    HTTP     HTTP     `yaml:"http"`
    Hosts    []string `initial:"a,b" yaml:"hosts" env:"HOSTS" doc:"allowed hosts"`
    Password string   `yaml:"password" env:"PASSWORD" hidden:"true"`
}

func main() {
    tagDriver, err := tag.New("initial") // defaults from the `initial` tag
    if err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }
    yamlDriver, err := yaml.New("config.yaml")
    if err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }
    envDriver, err := env.New()
    if err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }

    // the next driver overrides values of the previous one:
    // defaults < config.yaml < environment variables
    config, err := tinyconf.New(
        tinyconf.WithLogger(logger.NewFmtLogger(logger.INFO)),
        tinyconf.WithDriver(tagDriver),
        tinyconf.WithDriver(yamlDriver),
        tinyconf.WithDriver(envDriver),
    )
    if err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }

    c := &Config{}
    if err = config.Register(c); err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }
    if err = config.Parse(context.Background(), c); err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }
    fmt.Printf("%+v\n", *c)
}

With this config.yaml

http:
  port: 9090
password: secret

and HTTP_HOST=example.com in the environment the program prints

{HTTP:{Host:example.com Port:9090 Timeout:30s} Hosts:[a b] Password:secret}

Host came from the environment, Port and Password from the file, Timeout and Hosts from the defaults.

docs.title: Upgrading to v2
docs.text:
v2 changes the module path and a few methods. The steps for the code of v1:

  1. Change the imports from github.com/insei/tinyconf/... to github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/...:

    go get github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2@latest

  2. Parse takes the context: Parse(conf) is Parse(context.Background(), conf). The context stops the requests of the remote drivers.

  3. The zap adapter is the separate module, zap is not a dependency of the core anymore: logger.NewZapLogger(l) is zaplogger.New(l) from github.com/insei/tinyconf/logger/zaplogger, see Logging.

  4. Fields of an embedded struct without the tag are on the level of the embedding struct, like in encoding/json. Check the keys of such fields in the files and the environment variables.

docs.title: Use cases
docs.text:
Recipes for typical tasks. Every recipe is a small, complete piece: take the one that matches your application and combine it with others.

I want to… Recipe keep defaults next to the fields Defaults in code configure a service only by environment Environment only have a config file and override it by environment File with environment overrides have different files for dev, stage and prod Files per environment ship defaults inside the binary Embedded defaults keep secrets out of the files and logs Secrets run in Docker or Kubernetes Containers build a command line tool Command line tools set lists and maps from environment Lists and maps in environment have a section that can be absent Optional sections give every package its own config Config per package stop at start if something is missing Fail fast apply changes without restart Reload without restart keep the config in Consul Config in Consul generate an example of the config Config template find out where a value came from Debugging test the code that uses the config Tests read values from my own storage Custom source

All recipes use this helper to keep the examples short:

func must[T any](value T, err error) T {
    if err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }
    return value
}

docs.title: Defaults in code
docs.text:
Default values live in the tags, right next to the fields. The tag driver goes first, so every other driver can override it.

type Config struct {
    Host    string        `initial:"localhost"`
    Port    int           `initial:"8080"`
    Timeout time.Duration `initial:"30s"`
    Hosts   []string      `initial:"a,b"`
}

config := must(tinyconf.New(
    tinyconf.WithDriver(must(tag.New("initial"))),
))

A value that is computed at runtime can be set in the struct before Parse: the field keeps it, if no driver has a value.

c := &Config{Host: must(os.Hostname())}

docs.title: Environment only
docs.text:
A twelve-factor service without config files. With the auto keys the env tags are not needed, with the prefix the variables of the service do not clash with others.

type Config struct {
    HTTP struct {
        Host     string `initial:"0.0.0.0"`
        Port     int    `initial:"8080"`
        MaxConns int    `initial:"100"`
    }
    DatabaseURL string `required:"true" hidden:"true"`
}

config := must(tinyconf.New(
    tinyconf.WithDriver(must(tag.New("initial"))),
    tinyconf.WithDriver(must(env.New(env.WithPrefix("APP_"), env.WithAutoKeys()))),
))

APP_HTTP_PORT=9090
APP_HTTP_MAX_CONNS=500
APP_DATABASE_URL=postgres://db/app

docs.title: File with environment overrides
docs.text:
The most common setup: defaults, then a file, then the environment on top.

type Config struct {
    HTTP struct {
        Host string `initial:"localhost" yaml:"host" env:"HTTP_HOST"`
        Port int    `initial:"8080" yaml:"port" env:"HTTP_PORT"`
    } `yaml:"http"`
    LogLevel string `initial:"info" yaml:"log_level" env:"LOG_LEVEL"`
}

config := must(tinyconf.New(
    tinyconf.WithDriver(must(tag.New("initial"))),
    tinyconf.WithDriver(must(yaml.New("config.yaml", yaml.WithOptional()))),
    tinyconf.WithDriver(must(env.New())),
))

yaml.WithOptional() lets the application start without the file at all. Prefer JSON or TOML? The json and toml drivers have the same options, only the tag is different.

docs.title: Files per environment
docs.text:
One base file and a small file with differences for every environment. Files are merged: the next file overrides only the keys it has.

stage := os.Getenv("APP_ENV") // dev, stage, prod

yamlDriver := must(yaml.New("config.yaml",
    yaml.WithFiles(
        "config."+stage+".yaml",
        "config.local.yaml", // personal overrides, not in the repository
    ),
    yaml.WithOptional(),
))
config.yamlconfig.prod.yamlconfig.local.yaml 
http:
  host: 0.0.0.0
  port: 8080
log_level: info

log_level: warn

http:
  port: 9090
log_level: debug

docs.title: Embedded defaults
docs.text:
Defaults as a readable file that is compiled into the binary, with an optional external file on top. The binary works without any files around it.

//go:embed defaults.yaml
var defaults embed.FS

yamlDriver := must(yaml.New("",
    yaml.WithFS(defaults, "defaults.yaml"),
    yaml.WithFiles("/etc/app/config.yaml"),
    yaml.WithOptional(),
))

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
Three things protect a secret: it is not printed, it is not stored in the file, and the application does not start without it.

type Config struct {
    Database struct {
        Host     string `yaml:"host" env:"DB_HOST"`
        Password string `yaml:"password" env:"DB_PASSWORD" hidden:"true" required:"true"`
    } `yaml:"database"`
}
  • hidden:"true" masks the value in logs and removes it from GenDoc.
  • tinyconf.Secret instead of string masks the value when the application prints or logs the config itself: %+v, JSON, zap, slog.
  • required:"true" makes Parse fail without the value.

Where the value comes from:

Environment variableSecret fileReference in the config fileVault 
DB_PASSWORD=secret

env.New(env.WithSecretFiles())

# the value is read from the file
DB_PASSWORD_FILE=/run/secrets/db_password

yaml.New("config.yaml", yaml.WithEnvExpansion())

database:
  host: db.internal
  password: ${DB_PASSWORD}

// add after the file driver: the secret overrides the file
vault.New("app/database", vault.WithTokenFile("/vault/secrets/token"))

Password string `yaml:"password" vault:"password" hidden:"true" required:"true"`

The token is renewed by Vault Agent, see vault.

docs.title: Containers
docs.text:
A typical Kubernetes deployment: the config file is mounted from a ConfigMap, secrets are mounted as files, a few values are overridden by variables of the pod.

config := must(tinyconf.New(
    tinyconf.WithDriver(must(tag.New("initial"))),
    tinyconf.WithDriver(must(yaml.New("/etc/app/config.yaml",
        yaml.WithOptional(),
        yaml.WithWatchInterval(10*time.Second),
    ))),
    tinyconf.WithDriver(must(env.New(
        env.WithPrefix("APP_"),
        env.WithSecretFiles(), // APP_DB_PASSWORD_FILE=/run/secrets/db_password
        env.WithIndexedKeys(), // APP_HOSTS_0, APP_HOSTS_1
        env.WithFiles(),       // no .env files in the container
    ))),
))

env:
  - name: APP_DB_PASSWORD_FILE
    value: /run/secrets/db_password
  - name: APP_HOSTS_0
    value: a.example.com
  - name: APP_HOSTS_1
    value: b.example.com

A ConfigMap volume is updated by Kubernetes without restart of the pod, so the reloading picks up the changes of the file.

docs.title: Command line tools
docs.text:
Flags have the highest priority, the file and the environment provide the rest.

type Config struct {
    Output  string   `flag:"output" env:"TOOL_OUTPUT" initial:"out" doc:"output directory"`
    Include []string `flag:"include" doc:"patterns of files to include"`
    Verbose bool     `flag:"verbose" doc:"print debug messages"`
    Help    bool     `flag:"help" doc:"show this help"`
}

config := must(tinyconf.New(
    tinyconf.WithDriver(must(tag.New("initial"))),
    tinyconf.WithDriver(must(env.New())),
    tinyconf.WithDriver(must(flag.New())),
))

c := &Config{}
if err := config.Register(c); err != nil {
    panic(err)
}
if err := config.Parse(context.Background(), c); err != nil {
    fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
    os.Exit(2)
}
if c.Help {
    fmt.Print(config.GenDoc("flag"))
    return
}

tool --output=build --include='*.go' --include='*.md' --verbose

The driver ignores unknown flags, so it works next to any CLI framework that owns the sub commands and positional arguments.

docs.title: Lists and maps in environment
docs.text:
Three forms, from the shortest to the most flexible. All of them fill the same fields:

type Server struct {
    Host string `json:"host" env:"HOST"`
    Port int    `json:"port" env:"PORT"`
}

type Config struct {
    Hosts   []string          `env:"HOSTS"`
    Labels  map[string]string `env:"LABELS"`
    Servers []Server          `env:"SERVERS"`
}
SeparatorsJSONIndexed keys 
HOSTS=a.example.com,b.example.com
LABELS=env:prod,team:core

HOSTS='["a.example.com","b.example.com"]'
LABELS='{"env":"prod","team":"core"}'
SERVERS='[{"host":"a","port":1},{"host":"b","port":2}]'

HOSTS_0=a.example.com
HOSTS_1=b.example.com
LABELS_env=prod
LABELS_team=core
SERVERS_0_HOST=a
SERVERS_0_PORT=1
SERVERS_1_HOST=b
SERVERS_1_PORT=2

The indexed form requires env.WithIndexedKeys(). A value with the separator inside can be quoted, "a,b",c, or the separator can be changed with the separator tag.

docs.title: Optional sections
docs.text:
A feature that is turned on by the presence of its settings. The section is a struct stored by pointer: it stays nil until some driver has a value for one of its fields.

type TLS struct {
    Cert string `yaml:"cert" env:"TLS_CERT"`
    Key  string `yaml:"key" env:"TLS_KEY"`
}

type Metrics struct {
    Addr string `yaml:"addr" env:"METRICS_ADDR"`
}

type Config struct {
    TLS     *TLS     `yaml:"tls"`
    Metrics *Metrics `yaml:"metrics"`
}

if c.Metrics != nil {
    go serveMetrics(c.Metrics.Addr)
}
if c.TLS != nil {
    // TLS is enabled, but it can be set partially: check the fields
    if c.TLS.Cert == "" || c.TLS.Key == "" {
        return errors.New("both tls.cert and tls.key should be set")
    }
}

Do not use required:"true" inside an optional section: a required field is checked even when the section is nil, so it makes the whole section mandatory.

docs.title: Config per package
docs.text:
Every package declares the struct it needs and does not know about the whole config. The application registers the root config once and passes the manager around.

// package storage
type Config struct {
    DSN      string `yaml:"dsn" env:"STORAGE_DSN" required:"true" hidden:"true"`
    PoolSize int    `yaml:"pool_size" env:"STORAGE_POOL_SIZE" initial:"10"`
}

func New(config *tinyconf.Manager) (*Storage, error) {
    c := &Config{}
    if err := config.Parse(context.Background(), c); err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    return connect(c)
}

// package main
type Config struct {
    HTTP    server.Config  `yaml:"http"`
    Storage storage.Config `yaml:"storage"`
}

root := &Config{}
if err := config.Register(root); err != nil {
    panic(err)
}
store := must(storage.New(config)) // parses only the storage section

The package gets a sub config: its own fields with the keys of the whole config, storage.dsn in the file.

docs.title: Fail fast
docs.text:
Check everything at start and report all problems in one message.

if err := config.Parse(context.Background(), c); err != nil {
    if errors.Is(err, tinyconf.ErrRequired) {
        fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "some required settings are not set")
    }
    fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
    os.Exit(1)
}

env driver: field HTTP.Port: failed to parse ... "abc": invalid syntax; field Database.Password: required value is not set

Parse does not stop on the first error: incorrect values of all fields and all missing required fields are in the same error.

docs.title: Reload without restart
docs.text:
Every package subscribes to its own part of the config, the manager calls it only when this part is changed. See Reloading.

c := &Config{}
if err := config.Register(c); err != nil {
    panic(err)
}
if err := config.Parse(context.Background(), c); err != nil {
    panic(err)
}

err := tinyconf.Subscribe(ctx, config, func(prev, next *Logging) {
    if prev.Level != next.Level {
        setLogLevel(next.Level)
    }
})

Code that only reads the values takes the current version: tinyconf.Current[HTTP](config).Timeout. The versions are never modified, so they are read from any goroutine without locks.

docs.title: Config in Consul
docs.text:
The defaults are in the file next to the binary, the settings of the environment are in Consul, and the changes in Consul are applied without restart.

type Config struct {
    LogLevel string `yaml:"log_level" consul:"log_level"`
    HTTP     struct {
        Port int `yaml:"port" consul:"port"`
    } `yaml:"http" consul:"http"`
}

config := must(tinyconf.New(
    // the defaults and the shared document of all instances
    tinyconf.WithDriver(must(yaml.New("config.yaml",
        yaml.WithSource(consul.Document("app/config")),
    ))),
    // separate keys for quick changes: consul kv put app/log_level debug
    tinyconf.WithDriver(must(consul.New("app"))),
))

The address and the token are taken from CONSUL_HTTP_ADDR and CONSUL_HTTP_TOKEN, the same variables the Consul CLI uses. Subscribe to apply the changes: Consul notifies the driver right after the change. See consul.

docs.title: Config template
docs.text:
A flag that prints the example of the config and exits. The template is always up to date, because it is generated from the same structs.

c := &Config{}
if err := config.Register(c); err != nil {
    panic(err)
}
if len(os.Args) > 1 && os.Args[1] == "-doc" {
    // fills the defaults and the values of this environment,
    // missing required values are not a problem for the template
    _ = config.Parse(context.Background(), c)
    fmt.Println(config.GenDoc("yaml"))
    fmt.Println(config.GenDoc("env"))
    return
}

GenDoc shows the current values of the registered config, so after Parse the template has the defaults and everything that is set in this environment — it is also a "show effective config" command. Without Parse the template has empty values. Fields with hidden:"true" are never shown. See Documentation generation.

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
"Why is the port 9090?" Two tools answer it.

Sources shows the driver that has set the final value:

for _, source := range config.Sources(c) {
    log.Printf("%s is set by %s driver from %s", source.Field, source.Driver, source.Source)
}

HTTP.Host is set by env driver from HTTP_HOST
HTTP.Port is set by yaml driver from http.port

The logger on the debug level shows the history of every field: the initial value and every driver that has overridden it, then every change after reloads.

tinyconf.WithLogger(logger.NewFmtLogger(logger.DEBUG))

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Tests should not depend on the files and environment of the machine. Every driver can be fed from memory:

func newTestConfig(t *testing.T, yamlDoc string, args ...string) *Config {
    config := must(tinyconf.New(
        tinyconf.WithDriver(must(tag.New("initial"))),
        tinyconf.WithDriver(must(yaml.New("", yaml.WithData("test", []byte(yamlDoc))))),
        tinyconf.WithDriver(must(env.New(env.WithFiles()))), // no .env files
        tinyconf.WithDriver(must(flag.New(flag.WithArgs(args)))),
    ))
    c := &Config{}
    if err := config.Register(c); err != nil {
        t.Fatal(err)
    }
    if err := config.Parse(context.Background(), c); err != nil {
        t.Fatal(err)
    }
    return c
}

func TestPort(t *testing.T) {
    t.Setenv("HTTP_PORT", "7070")
    c := newTestConfig(t, "http:\n  host: test\n")
    // c.HTTP.Host == "test", c.HTTP.Port == 7070
}

To test with a .env file without changing the environment of the test process, use env.WithFiles(path) together with env.WithFilesIsolation().

docs.title: Custom source
docs.text:
Values from Vault, Consul, a database or any other storage: write a custom driver. Load reads the storage once per Parse, GetValue converts the values with the convert package, so the driver supports the same types as the bundled ones.

type kvDriver struct {
    client *kv.Client
    values map[string]string
}

func (d *kvDriver) GetName() string                       { return "kv" }
func (d *kvDriver) GenDoc(...*tinyconf.Registered) string { return "" }

func (d *kvDriver) Load() (err error) {
    d.values, err = d.client.FetchAll()
    return err
}

func (d *kvDriver) GetValue(field fmap.Field) (*tinyconf.Value, error) {
    key, ok := field.GetTag().Lookup("kv")
    if !ok {
        return nil, tinyconf.ErrIncorrectTagSettings
    }
    raw, ok := d.values[key]
    if !ok {
        return nil, tinyconf.ErrValueNotFound
    }
    value, err := convert.StringToField(raw, field)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    return &tinyconf.Value{Source: key, Value: value}, nil
}

Add the Watch method of the tinyconf.Watcher interface, and the driver takes part in reloading.

docs.title: Why tinyconf?
docs.text: Go has many config libraries: big key-value stores, struct-tag loaders, environment-only parsers. tinyconf occupies a specific niche: one config struct, filled by a chain of drivers, that tells you where every value came from and lets every package subscribe to its own part. This page lays out where it fits, what it gives up, and how it compares to the closest alternatives.

docs.title: The 30-second pitch
docs.text:
• The config is your struct. Every field says where its value lives: initial:"8080" yaml:"port" env:"HTTP_PORT" flag:"http-port". No key-value store in between, no Unmarshal step.
  • Drivers are a chain with priorities: defaults from tags, files, remote stores, environment, flags — the next driver overrides the previous one, field by field.
  • Every value has a history. Sources tells which driver and which key gave the final value; the debug log shows every override and every change after reloads. Secrets are masked everywhere.
  • Packages own their parts. A package parses or subscribes to its sub config by type — tinyconf.Subscribe(ctx, config, func(prev, next *HTTP) {...}) — and is called only when its part changes.
  • Documentation from the same structs: a YAML template, a .env file, flags help, consul kv put / vault kv put / etcdctl put commands — in the format of every driver.
  • Remote stores without heavy dependencies: Consul, Vault and etcd talk to their HTTP APIs directly; changes in Consul and etcd arrive right away, files are watched by the events of the file system.

docs.title: When to pick tinyconf
docs.text:
• Your service has several sources of config — defaults, a file, the environment, flags, a remote store — and you want one explicit priority order.
  • You want to answer "why is this value here?" from the logs, without guessing.
  • Your packages are independent: each one knows its own config struct, not the whole config.
  • You want config changes applied without restart, with the old config never modified under your readers.
  • You want the template of the config generated, not maintained by hand.

docs.title: When not to pick tinyconf
docs.text:
• You only read environment variables into a struct — caarlos0/env or sethvargo/go-envconfig have no dependencies at all.
  • You work with config as dynamic keys rather than a struct, or need many remote providers (S3, AWS Parameter Store and AppConfig, Azure Key Vault, NATS) out of the box — pick koanf.
  • You are deep in the cobra / pflag ecosystem — viper integrates with them directly.
  • You need Go older than 1.19.

docs.title: Strengths
docs.text:
• Provenance is built in. No other library from the table reports which source gave the final value of every field. With several drivers it is the difference between reading the logs and guessing. See Value sources and Logging.
  • Reloading that is safe to read. A reload builds a new version from the defaults, the old one is never modified, so readers need no locks. Subscribers are called only for their part and only with a config without errors; a broken file keeps the last good config. See Reloading.
  • The same types in every driver. time.Duration, url.URL, TextUnmarshaler, slices, maps, structs in lists and pointers behave the same in a file, an environment variable, a flag and a remote store — the conformance tests check it for the tag, yaml, json, toml, env and flag drivers, the other drivers share their conversion.
  • Remote stores without the weight. Consul, Vault and etcd drivers use their HTTP APIs: no SDKs, no gRPC. They handle the real-world cases — ACL that hides keys, expired tokens, compacted history, restarts of the store, failover between etcd endpoints — and are tested against real servers in Docker in CI.
  • Errors you can act on. Parse collects all errors of all fields at once; ErrAccessDenied separates permission problems from network ones; required:"true" fails fast at the start.
  • 100% test coverage, race detector and the minimal supported Go version in CI.

docs.title: Weaknesses
docs.text:
• Fewer remote stores than koanf. Consul, Vault and etcd only; others need a custom driver.
  • Vault: token authentication only. Kubernetes, AppRole and cloud login are delegated to Vault Agent; changes are detected by polling, because Vault does not notify.
  • No HCL out of the box. The format driver accepts any decoder, but the conversion of HCL to a map is up to you.
  • Own flag parser. It ignores unknown flags, so it lives next to cobra or any CLI framework, but it is not a pflag integration.
  • Subscriptions are package functions, tinyconf.Subscribe(ctx, config, ...), to keep Go 1.19 support; methods with type parameters need Go 1.27.
  • A younger and smaller project than viper and koanf.

docs.text:
From tinyconf v1: see Upgrading to v2.

From To tinyconf viper SetDefault("http.port", 8080) initial:"8080" with the tag driver viper AutomaticEnv() env.WithAutoKeys() viper WatchConfig() + OnConfigChange tinyconf.Subscribe per package viper Sub("http") config.Parse(context.Background(), &HTTP{}) or tinyconf.Current[HTTP](config) cleanenv env-default, env-required initial:"..." and required:"true" cleanenv env-description + Usage doc:"..." + GenDoc("env") caarlos0/env envDefault, required initial:"..." and required:"true"

docs.title: Drivers
docs.text:
A driver is a source of values. Every driver reads its own struct tag and knows how to find the value for the field in its source.

Driver Package Struct tag Source tag drivers/tag any, initial for example default values from struct tags yaml drivers/yaml yaml YAML files json drivers/json json JSON files toml drivers/toml toml TOML files ini drivers/ini ini INI files properties drivers/properties properties .properties files of Java and Spring env drivers/env env environment variables and .env files flag drivers/flag flag command line flags consul drivers/consul consul Consul KV: a key per field, or a document for yaml, json and toml vault drivers/vault vault secrets from the KV secrets engine of HashiCorp Vault etcd drivers/etcd etcd etcd: a key per field, or a document for yaml, json and toml

Drivers are added to the manager with tinyconf.WithDriver, the next driver overrides values of the previous one. All drivers support the same set of types.

Need another file format? See Custom formats: a decoder function is enough. Another source? See Custom drivers.

docs.title: consul
docs.text:
The consul package reads the config from Consul KV in two ways:

Way Where the config is Tags key per field every value in its own key: app/http/port consul document YAML, JSON or TOML document in one key: app/config of the format: yaml, json, toml

Both ways report changes for reloading as soon as they happen: the driver uses blocking queries of Consul, not polling. The package talks to the HTTP API of Consul directly and adds no dependencies.

docs.title: Key per field
docs.text:
import "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/drivers/consul"

consulDriver, err := consul.New("app")

The key of the field is the prefix and the path by the consul tags, dots are replaced with slashes:

type Config struct {
    HTTP struct {
        Host string `consul:"host"`
        Port int    `consul:"port"`
    } `consul:"http"`
    Hosts []string `consul:"hosts"`
}

consul kv put app/http/host example.com
consul kv put app/http/port 9090
consul kv put app/hosts a.example.com,b.example.com

Values are parsed by the rules of string values, like environment variables: slices are comma separated, structs in slices are JSON.

All keys with the prefix are read by one request once per Parse call. A key that is absent is not an error, the field keeps its value from the previous driver.

Set the tags of the parents

The key of the nested field is built from the consul tags of its parents. If the HTTP field has no consul tag, the Host field is read from app/host, not from app/http/host. When a value is found this way, the manager logs a warning. Embedded structs without the tag are the exception, their fields are on the level of the embedding struct.

docs.title: Document
docs.text:
consul.Document is a source of the config content for the yaml, json and toml drivers. The values are read by the tags of the format driver and merged with the files of the driver, as one more file:

yamlDriver, err := yaml.New("config.yaml",
    yaml.WithSource(consul.Document("app/config")),
)

consul kv put app/config @config.yaml

Here config.yaml has the defaults, and the document from Consul overrides them. An absent key is an error of Parse, unless the format driver has WithOptional().

docs.title: Connection
docs.text:
consulDriver, err := consul.New("app",
    consul.WithAddress("https://consul.service:8501"),
    consul.WithToken(token),
    consul.WithDatacenter("dc2"),
    consul.WithHTTPClient(&http.Client{Transport: tlsTransport}),
)
document := consul.Document("app/config", consul.WithAddress("consul.service:8500"))
Option Default Description WithAddress(address) CONSUL_HTTP_ADDR or 127.0.0.1:8500 host:port or URL with the scheme; without the scheme https is used if CONSUL_HTTP_SSL=true WithToken(token) CONSUL_HTTP_TOKEN ACL token WithDatacenter(dc) the datacenter of the agent datacenter of the keys WithHTTPClient(client) http.DefaultClient client with TLS settings, for example; its timeout should be greater than the wait time WithWaitTime(duration) 5 minutes maximum time of one blocking query, Consul limits it to 10 minutes

The options are the same for New and Document.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
With ACL Consul hides the keys that the token can not read, and answers as if they are absent. The driver does not let it make the config silently incomplete:

Case Result the token can not read the prefix error of Parse: 403 Forbidden the token can read only some keys with the prefix error of Parse: some keys are hidden by ACL the token can not read the key of the document error of Parse: 403 Forbidden access is denied while watching the driver stops watching, the error is logged: retries do not fix the permissions

All these errors wrap tinyconf.ErrAccessDenied: the manager logs them as access denied, and they can be checked with errors.Is. The token needs read on the prefix: key_prefix "app/" { policy = "read" }.

docs.title: Watching
docs.text:
The manager receives the changes of the keys with the prefix, or of the key of the document, right after they are written to Consul. Keys outside of the prefix do not cause reloads.

If Consul is not available, the driver keeps retrying the requests, with the interval that grows from 1 to 30 seconds, so a restart of Consul does not stop watching. After the failure the config is always reloaded: the changes made while Consul was not available are picked up, even if Consul has lost its data and started its indexes from scratch. The same is true for the start of the application: if Consul is not available at the first Parse, the values are loaded by the reloading as soon as Consul is available, and the subscribers are called.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
GenDoc("consul") generates the commands of the Consul CLI that put the current values to Consul KV, values of hidden:"true" fields are empty:

# http host
consul kv put app/http/host example.com
consul kv put app/http/port 9090
consul kv put app/hosts a.example.com,b.example.com

After Parse these are the values of the current environment: a way to move the config to Consul. For the document use GenDoc of the format driver.

docs.title: Custom drivers
docs.text:
Reading config files of another format? A decoder function and the format driver are enough, no custom driver is needed.

A driver is any type that implements the tinyconf.Driver interface:

type Driver interface {
    GenDoc(...*Registered) string
    GetName() string
    GetValue(field fmap.Field) (*Value, error)
}
Method Description GetName name of the driver, it is used in logs, errors and as an argument of Manager.GenDoc GetValue returns the value for the field, it is called for every field of the config GenDoc returns the documentation of the registered configs in the format of the driver, can return an empty string

docs.title: GetValue
docs.text:
The field is described by fmap.Field: GetTag() returns its struct tags, GetStructPath() — its path in the config, HTTP.Port for example.

The returned value should have exactly the type of the field. To support the same types as the bundled drivers, use the convert package:

  • convert.StringToField(s, field) — for sources with string values;
  • convert.TreeToField(v, field, tag) — for values decoded from formats like YAML or JSON.

The returned tinyconf.Value has three fields:

Field Description Value the value with the type of the field Source the key of the value in the source, HTTP_PORT or http.port for example; it is returned by Manager.Sources and logged as key Warning optional message for the user, the manager logs it with the Warn level; use it when the value is found, but probably not where the user expects

Two errors have a special meaning, all other errors are returned from Parse:

Error Meaning tinyconf.ErrIncorrectTagSettings the field has no settings for this driver, it is skipped tinyconf.ErrValueNotFound the source has no value for the field, the value of the previous driver is kept

Wrap tinyconf.ErrAccessDenied into the error if the source denies access: the token has no permission to read the values. It is still an error of Parse, but the manager logs it as access denied, so the problem with permissions is not lost among network errors, and the application can check it with errors.Is. Return it from Load, GetValue and Watch; Watch should stop on it, retries do not fix the permissions.

docs.title: Loader
docs.text:
GetValue is called for every field. If the source should be read once — a file, a response of the remote service — implement the optional tinyconf.Loader interface:

type Loader interface {
    Load() error
}

Load is called once at the start of every Parse call, before any GetValue call. If it returns an error, the driver is skipped in this Parse call and the error is returned from Parse.

A driver that reads its source by the network should implement tinyconf.ContextLoader instead: LoadContext gets the context of Parse, or the context of watching for reloads, and the requests should stop when it is done.

type ContextLoader interface {
    LoadContext(ctx context.Context) error
}

func (d *kvDriver) Load() error {
    values, err := d.client.FetchAll()
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    d.values = values
    return nil
}

docs.title: Watcher
docs.text:
A driver can report changes of its source for reloading by implementing the optional tinyconf.Watcher interface:

type Watcher interface {
    Watch(ctx context.Context, onChange func()) error
}

Watch should block until the context is done and call onChange after every change of the source. The manager parses the config again after the call, so Load and GetValue should return the new values.

func (d *kvDriver) Watch(ctx context.Context, onChange func()) error {
    events := d.client.Subscribe(ctx)
    for {
        select {
        case <-ctx.Done():
            return nil
        case <-events:
            onChange()
        }
    }
}

An error returned before the context is done is logged by the manager, and the driver does not take part in reloading anymore; other drivers continue watching.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
A driver that reads values from a map, the name of the value is taken from the kv tag:

type kvDriver struct {
    values map[string]string
}

func (d *kvDriver) GetName() string { return "kv" }

func (d *kvDriver) GenDoc(...*tinyconf.Registered) string { return "" }

func (d *kvDriver) GetValue(field fmap.Field) (*tinyconf.Value, error) {
    key, ok := field.GetTag().Lookup("kv")
    if !ok {
        return nil, tinyconf.ErrIncorrectTagSettings
    }
    raw, ok := d.values[key]
    if !ok {
        return nil, tinyconf.ErrValueNotFound
    }
    value, err := convert.StringToField(raw, field)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse %s: %w", key, err)
    }
    return &tinyconf.Value{Source: key, Value: value}, nil
}

type Config struct {
    Port  int      `kv:"port"`
    Hosts []string `kv:"hosts"`
}

config, err := tinyconf.New(tinyconf.WithDriver(&kvDriver{values: map[string]string{
    "port":  "8080",
    "hosts": "a,b",
}}))

docs.title: env
docs.text:
The env driver reads values from environment variables and .env files.

import "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/drivers/env"

envDriver, err := env.New()

docs.title: Names
docs.text:
The env tag is the name of the variable. Names are not built from the names of the parent structs, the variable is read exactly as it is written in the tag:

type Config struct {
    HTTP struct {
        Host string `env:"HTTP_HOST"`
        Port int    `env:"HTTP_PORT"`
    }
    Hosts []string `env:"HOSTS"`
}

HTTP_HOST=example.com
HTTP_PORT=9090
HOSTS=a.example.com,b.example.com

Values are parsed by the rules of string values.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
envDriver, err := env.New(
    env.WithPrefix("APP_"),
    env.WithAutoKeys(),
    env.WithSecretFiles(),
    env.WithFiles(".env", ".env.local"),
    env.WithFilesIsolation(),
    env.WithIndexedKeys(),
)
Option Description WithPrefix(prefix) adds the prefix to the names of all variables WithAutoKeys() reads the fields without the env tag, the name is built from the path of the field WithSecretFiles() reads the value from the file, if the variable with the _FILE suffix is set WithFiles(files...) custom .env files instead of the default ones WithFilesIsolation() does not export the values of the .env files to the process environment WithIndexedKeys() reads slices, arrays, maps and structs from separate variables

docs.title: Prefix
docs.text: With env.WithPrefix("APP_") the field with the env:"HTTP_PORT" tag is read from the APP_HTTP_PORT variable. It allows several applications to share one environment and keeps the tags short.

docs.title: Auto keys
docs.text:
With env.WithAutoKeys() the env tag is not required. The name of the variable is built from the struct path of the field:

Field Variable Name NAME HTTP.Port HTTP_PORT HTTP.MaxConns HTTP_MAX_CONNS DBName DB_NAME HTTP.Timeouts.Read, Timeouts is embedded HTTP_READ

The env tag still has priority, and the field can be excluded with env:"-".

docs.title: Secret files
docs.text:
Docker and Kubernetes mount secrets as files. With env.WithSecretFiles() the value can be read from such file: if the HTTP_TOKEN variable is not set, but HTTP_TOKEN_FILE is set, the value is read from the file with the path from HTTP_TOKEN_FILE.

type Config struct {
    Token string `env:"HTTP_TOKEN" hidden:"true"`
}

HTTP_TOKEN_FILE=/run/secrets/http_token

The trailing line break of the file content is removed. The variable with the value itself has priority over the file.

docs.title: Indexed keys
docs.text:
By default, a slice, a map or a list of structs is set by one variable with the whole value: HOSTS=a,b or JSON. With env.WithIndexedKeys() every item can have its own variable. It is the form that is natural for Kubernetes manifests and Docker Compose files, where a long JSON in one variable is hard to read and to override.

type Server struct {
    Host     string `env:"HOST"`
    MaxConns int
    Tags     []string
}

type Config struct {
    Hosts   []string          `env:"HOSTS"`
    Labels  map[string]string `env:"LABELS"`
    Servers []Server          `env:"SERVERS"`
}
Type Variables Hosts []string HOSTS_0=a, HOSTS_1=b Labels map[string]string LABELS_env=prod, LABELS_team=core Servers []Server SERVERS_0_HOST=a, SERVERS_0_MAX_CONNS=10, SERVERS_0_TAGS_0=x, SERVERS_1_HOST=b

Rules:

  • Slices and arrays — the index is added to the name of the field. Indexes should be sequential and start from 0, a gap is an error.
  • Maps — the rest of the name after the prefix is a key, as is, case-sensitive.
  • Structs inside slices and maps — names of the fields are taken from their env tags or built from the field names: MaxConns is MAX_CONNS. Fields with env:"-" are skipped.
  • Nesting is not limited: SERVERS_0_TAGS_0 is the first tag of the first server.
  • The variable with the whole value has priority: if HOSTS is set, HOSTS_0 is ignored.
  • The prefix is added to all names: APP_HOSTS_0.

Names of the map fields

For a map with simple values every variable started with the name of the field and _ becomes an item of the map. With Labels read from LABELS, the variable LABELS_FILE is the FILE key. Choose the name of such field so that it is not a prefix of other variables.

docs.title: .env files
docs.text:
By default, env.New reads the .env files from the directory of the executable and from the working directory and exports their values to the process environment. Absent default files are skipped.

# comment
HTTP_HOST=example.com
TOKEN="quoted value"
  • Empty lines and lines started with # are skipped.
  • Matching single or double quotes around the value are removed.
  • Variables that are already set in the process environment are not overridden, so the real environment has priority over the files.

docs.title: Custom files
docs.text:
env.New(env.WithFiles(".env", ".env.local"))

WithFiles replaces the default files. All listed files should exist, otherwise env.New returns an error. The value from the previous file has priority over the next files, and the process environment has priority over all files.

env.WithFiles() without arguments disables reading of the .env files at all.

docs.title: Isolation
docs.text: Exported values are visible to the whole process and to its child processes. With env.WithFilesIsolation() the values of the files are available only for the driver, os.Getenv does not see them. It is also useful in tests, where the changed environment of the process is a side effect.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: GenDoc("env") generates a commented template of the .env file, see Documentation generation. Names of the variables are shown with the prefix, fields without the env tag are included if the auto keys are enabled.

docs.title: etcd
docs.text:
The etcd package reads the config from etcd version 3 in two ways:

Way Where the config is Tags key per field every value in its own key: app/http/port etcd document YAML, JSON or TOML document in one key: app/config of the format: yaml, json, toml

Both ways report changes for reloading as soon as they happen: the driver watches the keys by the stream of the events of etcd, not by polling. The package talks to the gRPC gateway of etcd — its JSON API — directly and adds no dependencies.

docs.title: Key per field
docs.text:
import "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/drivers/etcd"

etcdDriver, err := etcd.New("app")

The key of the field is the prefix and the path by the etcd tags, dots are replaced with slashes:

type Config struct {
    HTTP struct {
        Host string `etcd:"host"`
        Port int    `etcd:"port"`
    } `etcd:"http"`
    Hosts []string `etcd:"hosts"`
}

etcdctl put app/http/host example.com
etcdctl put app/http/port 9090
etcdctl put app/hosts a.example.com,b.example.com

Values are parsed by the rules of string values, like environment variables: slices are comma separated, structs in slices are JSON.

All keys with the prefix are read by one request once per Parse call. A key that is absent is not an error, the field keeps its value from the previous driver.

Set the tags of the parents

The key of the nested field is built from the etcd tags of its parents. If the HTTP field has no etcd tag, the Host field is read from app/host, not from app/http/host. When a value is found this way, the manager logs a warning. Embedded structs without the tag are the exception.

docs.title: Document
docs.text:
etcd.Document is a source of the config content for the yaml, json and toml drivers. The values are read by the tags of the format driver and merged with the files of the driver, as one more file:

yamlDriver, err := yaml.New("config.yaml",
    yaml.WithSource(etcd.Document("app/config")),
)

etcdctl put app/config < config.yaml

An absent key is an error of Parse, unless the format driver has WithOptional().

docs.title: Connection
docs.text:
etcdDriver, err := etcd.New("app",
    etcd.WithEndpoints("https://etcd-1:2379", "https://etcd-2:2379", "https://etcd-3:2379"),
    etcd.WithAuth("app", password),
    etcd.WithHTTPClient(&http.Client{Transport: tlsTransport}),
)
document := etcd.Document("app/config", etcd.WithEndpoints("etcd:2379"))
Option Default Description WithEndpoints(endpoints...) ETCDCTL_ENDPOINTS or http://127.0.0.1:2379 host:port or URL with the scheme; the variable is comma separated WithAuth(user, password) ETCDCTL_USER (user or user:password) and ETCDCTL_PASSWORD the user for the clusters with authentication WithHTTPClient(client) http.DefaultClient the client with TLS settings and client certificates, for example

The options are the same for New and Document, and the variables are the same as etcdctl uses.

Requests go to the next endpoint if the current one is not available, and the endpoint that has answered is used first next time. A cluster keeps working for the application while it has the quorum.

With the user the driver gets the token of etcd and gets it again when the token is expired.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
Case Result authentication is enabled, the user is not set error of Parse: user name is empty wrong password error of Parse: authentication failed the user can not read the prefix or the key error of Parse: permission denied access is denied while watching the driver stops watching, the error is logged: retries do not fix the permissions

All these errors wrap tinyconf.ErrAccessDenied: the manager logs them as access denied, and they can be checked with errors.Is. The role of the user needs read on the prefix: etcdctl role grant-permission --prefix=true app read app/.

docs.title: Watching
docs.text:
The manager receives the changes of the keys with the prefix, or of the key of the document, right after they are written to etcd. Keys outside of the prefix do not cause reloads.

If the stream of the events is broken, the driver watches again from the last known revision, with the interval that grows from 1 to 30 seconds, so no changes are missed. If the history of the changes is already compacted, the config is reloaded from the current state. The same is true for the start of the application: if etcd is not available at the first Parse, the values are loaded by the reloading as soon as etcd is available, and the subscribers are called.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
GenDoc("etcd") generates the commands of etcdctl that put the current values to etcd, values of hidden:"true" fields are empty:

# http host
etcdctl put -- app/http/host example.com
etcdctl put -- app/http/port 9090
etcdctl put -- app/hosts a.example.com,b.example.com

After Parse these are the values of the current environment: a way to move the config to etcd. For the document use GenDoc of the format driver.

docs.title: flag
docs.text:
The flag driver reads values from command line flags.

import "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/drivers/flag"

flagDriver, err := flag.New()

Add it last, so the flags have the highest priority:

config, err := tinyconf.New(
    tinyconf.WithDriver(tagDriver),
    tinyconf.WithDriver(yamlDriver),
    tinyconf.WithDriver(envDriver),
    tinyconf.WithDriver(flagDriver),
)

docs.title: Names
docs.text:
The flag tag is the name of the flag without dashes:

type Config struct {
    HTTP struct {
        Host string `flag:"http-host" doc:"http host"`
        Port int    `flag:"http-port" doc:"http port"`
    }
    Hosts   []string `flag:"host" doc:"allowed hosts"`
    Verbose bool     `flag:"verbose"`
}

app --http-host=example.com --http-port 9090 --host=a --host=b -verbose

A field without the flag tag is not read from the command line.

docs.title: Supported forms
docs.text:
Form Example -name=value, --name=value --http-port=9090 -name value, --name value --http-port 9090 -name, --name for bool fields --verbose
  • Bool fields do not take the next argument as a value: use --verbose=false to set false.
  • Slices and arrays can be filled with repeated flags: --host=a --host=b,c is [a b c]. For all other types the last occurrence of the flag is used.
  • All arguments after -- are ignored.
  • Values are parsed by the rules of string values.

docs.title: Unknown flags
docs.text:
The driver does not own the command line: it only looks for the flags of the config fields. Unknown flags and positional arguments are ignored, so the driver can be used together with the flag package of the standard library or with any CLI framework.

No --help

The driver does not handle -h and --help. Print GenDoc("flag") from your own handler of the help flag.

docs.title: Custom arguments
docs.text:
By default os.Args[1:] is used. Custom arguments are set with WithArgs, in tests or for sub commands:

flagDriver, err := flag.New(flag.WithArgs(os.Args[2:]))

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
GenDoc("flag") generates the usage of all flags with descriptions from the doc tags and current values as defaults:

  -http-host
        http host (default example.com)
  -http-port
        http port (default 9090)
  -host
        allowed hosts (default a,b)
  -verbose
         (default false)

Values of the fields with hidden:"true" are not shown.

docs.title: Custom formats
docs.text:
The format driver reads config files of any format with nested objects. The format is set by a function that decodes the content to a map, everything else is the same as in the yaml, json and toml drivers: several files, merging, embedded files, remote documents, environment variables in the content, reloading, documentation.

import "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/drivers/format"

driver, err := format.New("hujson", decodeHuJSON, "config.hujson")

The name of the driver is the name of the struct tag with the keys, and the name for GenDoc:

type Config struct {
    HTTP struct {
        Port int `hujson:"port"`
    } `hujson:"http"`
}

docs.title: Decoder
docs.text:
type Decoder func(data []byte) (map[string]any, error)

The decoder returns the content as a map:

  • keys of the map are the keys of the config, nested maps with string keys are nested objects;
  • slices are lists, other values are scalars: strings, numbers, booleans, time.Time;
  • empty content can be decoded to a nil map.

Values are converted to the types of the fields by the same rules as the values of yaml and json, see Supported types.

For example, HuJSON — JSON with comments and trailing commas:

import "github.com/tailscale/hujson"

func decodeHuJSON(data []byte) (map[string]any, error) {
    data, err := hujson.Standardize(data)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    var doc map[string]any
    return doc, json.Unmarshal(data, &doc)
}

Libraries that decode to the structs only, like HCL, need the conversion of their result to the map.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Option Description WithFiles(files...) additional files from the OS file system WithFS(fsys, files...) files from any fs.FS, embed.FS for example WithData(name, data) in-memory content, the name is used in error messages WithSource(source) content from a remote storage: consul.Document, etcd.Document WithOptional() files can be absent WithEnvExpansion() replaces ${VAR} in the content with environment variables WithWatchInterval(interval) interval of polling the files for reloading, 5 seconds by default WithEncoder(encode) encoder of the documents for GenDoc

The rules of the files are the same as in the yaml driver.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
GenDoc needs the encoder:

type Encoder func(doc map[string]any) ([]byte, error)

driver, err := format.New("hujson", decodeHuJSON, "config.hujson", format.WithEncoder(func(doc map[string]any) ([]byte, error) {
    return json.MarshalIndent(doc, "", "  ")
}))

The document has the same structure as the result of the decoder, with the current values of the registered configs; values of hidden:"true" fields are empty strings. Without the encoder GenDoc returns an empty string.

docs.title: Not a file format?
docs.text: If the values are not stored as documents — a database, an API, a secret manager — write a custom driver.

docs.title: ini
docs.text:
The ini driver reads values from INI files.

import "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/drivers/ini"

iniDriver, err := ini.New("config.ini")

The driver has its own parser and adds no dependencies.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text:
The ini tag is a key in the file. Tags of nested structs are sections:

type Config struct {
    Name string `ini:"name"`
    HTTP struct {
        Host string `ini:"host"`
        Port int    `ini:"port"`
        TLS  struct {
            Cert string `ini:"cert"`
        } `ini:"tls"`
    } `ini:"http"`
}

name = app

[http]
host = example.com
port = 9090

[http.tls]
cert = /etc/tls/cert.pem

Dots in the names of the sections and in the keys are nested objects: [http.tls] is the tls object inside http, and http.port = 9090 in the root is the same as port = 9090 in the [http] section.

Set the tags of the parents

The path of the nested field is built from the ini tags of its parents. If the HTTP field has no ini tag, the Host field is read from the host key in the root of the file, and the manager logs a warning. Embedded structs without the tag are the exception.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
Element Example key and value port = 9090, port: 9090 section [http], [http.tls] comment ; comment, # comment comment after the value port = 9090 ; comment, after a space value in double quotes, with escapes name = "my \"app\"\n" value in single quotes, as is name = 'my app; # not a comment' empty value name =

Values of INI are strings, they are parsed by the rules of string values like environment variables: true, 9090, 1m30s; lists are comma separated hosts = a,b, maps are labels = env:prod,team:core, structs in lists are JSON with the keys by the ini tags: servers = '[{"host": "a", "port": 1}]'. A map can be a section too:

[labels]
env = prod
team = core

A key can not be a value and a section at the same time: http = 1 and [http] in one file is an error of Parse with the number of the line.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
The options are the same as of the yaml driver:

Option Description WithFiles(files...) additional files from the OS file system WithFS(fsys, files...) files from any fs.FS, embed.FS for example WithData(name, data) in-memory content, the name is used in error messages WithSource(source) content from a remote storage: consul.Document, etcd.Document WithOptional() files can be absent WithEnvExpansion() replaces ${VAR} in the content with environment variables WithWatchInterval(interval) interval of polling the files for reloading, 5 seconds by default; changes are detected by the events of the file system without waiting for it

Files are merged in the order of addition, sections are merged by keys.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
GenDoc("ini") generates the INI file with the current values: the values of the root first, then the sections of the nested structs. Values of hidden:"true" fields are empty, the values that need it are quoted, so the file is read back to the same config.

hosts = a,b
name = 'my app; with comment chars'

[http]
host = example.com
port = 9090

docs.title: json
docs.text:
The json driver reads values from JSON files.

import "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/drivers/json"

jsonDriver, err := json.New("config.json")

docs.title: Keys
docs.text:
The json tag is a key in the file. Tags of nested structs are keys of nested objects:

type Config struct {
    Name string `json:"name"`
    HTTP struct {
        Host string `json:"host"`
        Port int    `json:"port"`
    } `json:"http"`
    Hosts []string `json:"hosts"`
}

{
  "name": "app",
  "http": {
    "host": "example.com",
    "port": 9090
  },
  "hosts": ["a", "b"]
}

Options after the comma are ignored: json:"port,omitempty" is the port key. Set the json tag on all parents of the field: without the tag of the parent the field is read from the root of the file, and the manager logs a warning. Embedded structs without the tag are the exception, their fields are on the level of the embedding struct.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
The options are the same as in the yaml driver:

jsonDriver, err := json.New("config.json",
    json.WithFiles("config.local.json"),
    json.WithOptional(),
    json.WithEnvExpansion(),
)
Option Description WithFiles(files...) additional files from the OS file system WithFS(fsys, files...) files from any fs.FS, embed.FS for example WithData(name, data) in-memory content, the name is used in error messages WithSource(source) content from a remote storage: consul.Document WithOptional() files can be absent WithEnvExpansion() replaces ${VAR} and ${VAR:-default} in the content with environment variables WithWatchInterval(interval) interval of polling the files for reloading, 5 seconds by default; changes are detected by the events of the file system without waiting for it

Several files are merged in the order of addition, objects are merged by keys. Files are read once per Parse call.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
GenDoc("json") generates a JSON document with all fields and their current values:

{
  "hosts": [
    "a",
    "b"
  ],
  "http": {
    "host": "example.com",
    "port": 9090
  },
  "name": "app"
}

JSON has no comments, so the doc tags are not used. Values of the fields with hidden:"true" are replaced with empty strings.

docs.title: properties
docs.text:
The properties driver reads values from .properties files — the format of Java and Spring, application.properties.

import "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/drivers/properties"

propertiesDriver, err := properties.New("application.properties")

The driver has its own parser and adds no dependencies.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text:
The properties tag is a part of the key. Tags of nested structs are the parts before the dots:

type Config struct {
    Name string `properties:"name"`
    HTTP struct {
        Host string `properties:"host"`
        Port int    `properties:"port"`
    } `properties:"http"`
}

name=app
http.host=example.com
http.port=9090

Set the tags of the parents

The key of the nested field is built from the properties tags of its parents. If the HTTP field has no properties tag, the Host field is read from the host key, and the manager logs a warning. Embedded structs without the tag are the exception.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
The syntax of java.util.Properties:

Element Example key and value port=9090, port: 9090, port 9090 comment # comment, ! comment escapes \t, \n, \r, \f, \\, \uXXXX; \ before any other character is the character separators and spaces in keys key\ with\=separators=value long value on several lines a backslash at the end of the line, the leading spaces of the next line are skipped

The spaces before the value are skipped, the spaces at the end are a part of the value, like in Java.

Values are strings, they are parsed by the rules of string values like environment variables: true, 9090, 1m30s; lists are comma separated hosts=a,b, maps are labels=env:prod,team:core or the keys labels.env=prod, structs in lists are JSON with the keys by the properties tags: servers=[{"host": "a", "port": 1}].

A key can not be a value and an object at the same time: http=1 and http.port=2 in one file is an error of Parse with the number of the line.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
The options are the same as of the yaml driver:

Option Description WithFiles(files...) additional files from the OS file system: application-prod.properties WithFS(fsys, files...) files from any fs.FS, embed.FS for example WithData(name, data) in-memory content, the name is used in error messages WithSource(source) content from a remote storage: consul.Document, etcd.Document WithOptional() files can be absent WithEnvExpansion() replaces ${VAR} in the content with environment variables WithWatchInterval(interval) interval of polling the files for reloading, 5 seconds by default; changes are detected by the events of the file system without waiting for it

Files are merged in the order of addition, like the profiles of Spring:

propertiesDriver, err := properties.New("application.properties",
    properties.WithFiles("application-"+profile+".properties"),
    properties.WithOptional(),
)

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
GenDoc("properties") generates the file with the current values, sorted by the keys. Values of hidden:"true" fields are empty, the special characters are escaped, so the file is read back to the same config.

http.host=example.com
http.port=9090
name=app

docs.title: tag
docs.text:
The tag driver takes values right from the struct tags. It is used for default values.

import "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/drivers/tag"

tagDriver, err := tag.New("initial")

The argument is the name of the tag with values, any name can be used: initial, default.

type Config struct {
    Host    string        `initial:"localhost"`
    Port    int           `initial:"8080"`
    Timeout time.Duration `initial:"30s"`
    Hosts   []string      `initial:"a,b"`
}

Add it first, so all other drivers can override the defaults:

config, err := tinyconf.New(
    tinyconf.WithDriver(tagDriver),
    tinyconf.WithDriver(yamlDriver),
    tinyconf.WithDriver(envDriver),
)

Values are parsed by the rules of string values. An incorrect default value is an error of Parse, so a typo in the tag is found at the first start.

The driver has no own documentation format, GenDoc returns an empty string for it. Default values are visible in the documentation of other drivers as the values of the fields.

docs.title: toml
docs.text:
The toml driver reads values from TOML files.

import "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/drivers/toml"

tomlDriver, err := toml.New("config.toml")

docs.title: Keys
docs.text:
The toml tag is a key in the file. Tags of nested structs are names of tables:

type Server struct {
    Host string `toml:"host"`
    Port int    `toml:"port"`
}

type Config struct {
    Name string `toml:"name"`
    HTTP struct {
        Host    string        `toml:"host"`
        Timeout time.Duration `toml:"timeout"`
    } `toml:"http"`
    Hosts   []string          `toml:"hosts"`
    Labels  map[string]string `toml:"labels"`
    Servers []Server          `toml:"servers"`
}

name = "app"
hosts = ["a", "b"]

[http]
host = "example.com"
timeout = "30s"

[labels]
env = "prod"

[[servers]]
host = "a"
port = 1

[[servers]]
host = "b"
port = 2

Set the toml tag on all parents of the field: without the tag of the parent the field is read from the root of the file, and the manager logs a warning. Embedded structs without the tag are the exception, their fields are on the level of the embedding struct. Native TOML dates are supported for time.Time fields.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
The options are the same as in the yaml driver:

tomlDriver, err := toml.New("config.toml",
    toml.WithFiles("config.local.toml"),
    toml.WithOptional(),
    toml.WithEnvExpansion(),
)
Option Description WithFiles(files...) additional files from the OS file system WithFS(fsys, files...) files from any fs.FS, embed.FS for example WithData(name, data) in-memory content, the name is used in error messages WithSource(source) content from a remote storage: consul.Document WithOptional() files can be absent WithEnvExpansion() replaces ${VAR} and ${VAR:-default} in the content with environment variables WithWatchInterval(interval) interval of polling the files for reloading, 5 seconds by default; changes are detected by the events of the file system without waiting for it

Several files are merged in the order of addition, tables are merged by keys. Files are read once per Parse call.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
GenDoc("toml") generates a TOML document with all fields and their current values:

hosts = ["a", "b"]
name = "app"

[http]
  host = "example.com"
  timeout = "30s"

[labels]
  env = "prod"
  • The doc tags are not used.
  • Values of the fields with hidden:"true" are replaced with empty strings.
  • TOML has no null, so nil pointers and other fields without values are skipped.

docs.title: vault
docs.text:
The vault driver reads values from the KV secrets engine of HashiCorp Vault.

import "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/drivers/vault"

vaultDriver, err := vault.New("app/config")

The driver talks to the HTTP API of Vault directly and adds no dependencies.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text:
A secret in Vault is a JSON object. The vault tag is a key in it, tags of nested structs are keys of nested objects:

type Config struct {
    Database struct {
        Host     string `vault:"host"`
        Password string `vault:"password" hidden:"true"`
    } `vault:"database"`
    Hosts []string `vault:"hosts"`
}

vault kv put -mount=secret app/config - <<'EOF'
{"database": {"host": "db.internal", "password": "secret"}, "hosts": ["a", "b"]}
EOF

Values of the secret can be JSON values or strings: "port": 5432 and "port": "5432" are the same for an int field, "timeout": "1m30s" is a time.Duration, see Supported types.

Set the tags of the parents

The path of the nested field is built from the vault tags of its parents. If the Database field has no vault tag, the Password field is read from the password key in the root of the secret, and the manager logs a warning. Embedded structs without the tag are the exception.

docs.title: Several secrets
docs.text:
vaultDriver, err := vault.New("app/config", vault.WithPaths("app/database", "shared/certificates"))

Secrets are merged in the order of addition, like several files: values from the next secret override values from the previous one, nested objects are merged by keys. It is a common layout: the settings and the credentials in different secrets with different access policies.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
vaultDriver, err := vault.New("app/config",
    vault.WithAddress("https://vault.internal:8200"),
    vault.WithTokenFile("/vault/secrets/token"),
    vault.WithMount("kv"),
)
Option Default Description WithAddress(address) VAULT_ADDR or https://127.0.0.1:8200 URL of Vault WithToken(token) VAULT_TOKEN the token WithTokenFile(path) the file with the token, it is read before every request WithNamespace(namespace) VAULT_NAMESPACE the namespace of Vault Enterprise WithMount(mount) secret the mount of the KV secrets engine WithKVv1() KV version 2 read from the KV secrets engine version 1 WithHTTPClient(client) http.DefaultClient the client with TLS settings, for example WithPaths(paths...) additional secrets WithOptional() secrets can be absent, by default an absent secret is an error WithWatchInterval(interval) 30 seconds the interval of checking the secrets for changes

The first argument of New can be an empty string, if the secrets are set by WithPaths.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
The driver uses a token. Other methods — Kubernetes, AppRole, cloud IAM — are handled by Vault Agent: it logs in, renews the token and writes it to the file. Point the driver to this file:

vaultDriver, err := vault.New("app/config", vault.WithTokenFile("/vault/secrets/token"))

The file is read before every request, so the renewed token is used without restart of the application.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Case Result the secret is absent error of Parse, unless WithOptional() the token can not read the secret error of Parse that wraps tinyconf.ErrAccessDenied, logged as access denied Vault is not available or sealed error of Parse

The driver is skipped in the Parse call with the error, see Missing files and values.

docs.title: Reloading
docs.text:
Vault does not notify about changes, so the driver checks the versions of the secrets every 30 seconds while there are subscriptions. The interval is set with WithWatchInterval. A secret that appears, disappears or becomes available again after an error is a change too.

For KV version 2 the version of the secret is checked, for KV version 1 — the hash of its data.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
GenDoc("vault") generates the command of the Vault CLI that puts the current values to the first secret, values of hidden:"true" fields are empty:

vault kv put -mount=secret app/config - <<'EOF'
{
  "database": {
    "host": "db.internal",
    "password": ""
  },
  "hosts": [
    "a",
    "b"
  ]
}
EOF

docs.title: yaml
docs.text:
The yaml driver reads values from YAML files.

import "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/drivers/yaml"

yamlDriver, err := yaml.New("config.yaml")

docs.title: Keys
docs.text:
The yaml tag is a key in the file. Tags of nested structs are keys of nested maps:

type Config struct {
    Name string `yaml:"name"`
    HTTP struct {
        Host string `yaml:"host"`
        Port int    `yaml:"port"`
    } `yaml:"http"`
}

name: app
http:
  host: example.com
  port: 9090

Options after the comma are ignored: yaml:"port,omitempty" is the port key.

Set the tags of the parents

The path of the nested field is built from the yaml tags of its parents. If the HTTP field has no yaml tag, the Host field is read from the host key in the root of the file, not from http.host.

When a value is found this way, the manager logs a warning with the name of the parent without the tag and the key that was used.

Embedded structs are the exception: they do not need the tag, their fields are on the level of the embedding struct.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
yamlDriver, err := yaml.New("config.yaml",
    yaml.WithFiles("config.local.yaml"),
    yaml.WithOptional(),
    yaml.WithEnvExpansion(),
)
Option Description WithFiles(files...) additional files from the OS file system WithFS(fsys, files...) files from any fs.FS, embed.FS for example WithData(name, data) in-memory content, the name is used in error messages WithSource(source) content from a remote storage: consul.Document WithOptional() files can be absent WithEnvExpansion() replaces ${VAR} in the content with environment variables WithWatchInterval(interval) interval of polling the files for reloading, 5 seconds by default; changes are detected by the events of the file system without waiting for it

The first argument of New can be an empty string, if all sources are set by options.

docs.title: Several files
docs.text:
Sources are merged in the order of addition: the file from New first, then the sources from options in the order of the options. Values from the next source override values from the previous one, nested maps are merged by keys, all other values — lists too — are replaced.

config.yamlconfig.local.yamlResult 
http:
  host: example.com
  port: 80
hosts: [a, b]

http:
  port: 9090
hosts: [c]

http:
  host: example.com
  port: 9090
hosts: [c]

It is a base for the layered configs: defaults embedded into the binary, the main file, the local overrides.

//go:embed defaults.yaml
var defaults embed.FS

yamlDriver, err := yaml.New("",
    yaml.WithFS(defaults, "defaults.yaml"),
    yaml.WithFiles("/etc/app/config.yaml", "config.local.yaml"),
    yaml.WithOptional(),
)

docs.title: Missing files and values
docs.text:
A key that is absent in the files is not an error, the field keeps its value from the previous driver.

A file that can not be read is an error of Parse, and the driver is skipped in this Parse call. With WithOptional() absent files are skipped silently, all other errors — a directory instead of the file, incorrect YAML — are still returned.

docs.title: Environment variables in files
docs.text:
With WithEnvExpansion() the content of the files is processed before decoding:

Syntax Result ${VAR} value of the variable, empty string if it is not set ${VAR:-default} value of the variable, default if it is not set or empty $$ the $ sign 
database:
  host: ${DB_HOST:-localhost}
  password: ${DB_PASSWORD}

docs.title: Reading
docs.text: Files are read once per Parse call, not for every field. The next Parse call rereads them, so the changed file is picked up without recreation of the driver.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: GenDoc("yaml") generates a commented template of the file, see Documentation generation.

docs.text:
Reference of tinyconf capabilities grouped by area.

Looking for a recipe?

The Use cases page shows how the features work together in typical setups: a twelve-factor service, a config file with overrides, a command line tool, a Kubernetes deployment.
