docs.text: Page What's inside Documentation generation GenDoc: a config template in the format of the driver Value sources Sources: which driver has set the value of every field Reloading Subscribe and Current: configs are parsed again after changes of the sources Logging What the manager logs, bundled loggers, custom logger

docs.title: Documentation generation
docs.text:
GenDoc(driverName) generates a template of the config in the format of the driver: all fields of all registered configs with their descriptions and current values.

c := &Config{}
if err := config.Register(c); err != nil {
    panic(err)
}
if err := config.Parse(context.Background(), c); err != nil {
    panic(err)
}
fmt.Println(config.GenDoc("yaml"))
fmt.Println(config.GenDoc("env"))

For this config

type HTTP struct {
    Host string `yaml:"host" env:"HTTP_HOST" initial:"localhost" doc:"http host"`
    Port int    `yaml:"port" env:"HTTP_PORT" initial:"8080" doc:"http port"`
}

type Config struct {
    HTTP     HTTP   `yaml:"http"`
    Password string `yaml:"password" env:"PASSWORD" hidden:"true"`
}

the output is

yamlenv 
#
#http: 
    #http host
    #host: localhost
    #http port
    #port: 8080
#
#password: 

#http host
#HTTP_HOST=localhost
#http port
#HTTP_PORT=8080

#
#PASSWORD=
  • The description is taken from the doc tag.
  • The value is the current value of the field in the registered config, so call GenDoc after Parse to get the actual values, or before it to get a clean template.
  • Values of the fields with hidden:"true" are not shown.
  • Slices and maps are shown in the format of the driver: hosts: ["a","b"] for yaml, HOSTS=a,b for env, so the value can be copied from the template as is.
  • The name of the driver is the name of its tag: yaml, json, toml, ini, properties, env, flag, consul, vault, etcd. The consul, vault and etcd drivers generate the commands of their CLI, see consul, vault and etcd.
  • The json and toml drivers generate documents without descriptions, see json and toml.

A common way to use it is a command line flag of the application that prints the template and exits.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
The manager logs what happens with every field during Parse.

Level Message Debug initial: the value of the field before drivers; override: the value is overridden by the driver; skip: the driver has no value for the field Warn the field has no tag of the driver; the driver has found the value in an unexpected place Error access denied: the source denies access to the values, tinyconf.ErrAccessDenied; failed, failed to load, failed to watch: the driver failed to get, to parse or to watch the values

Messages have the fields config, driver, field, key and details or value. Values of the fields with hidden:"true" are masked.

docs.title: History of a field
docs.text:
On the debug level the log has the whole history of every field: grep the log by the name of the field to see where its value came from.

  • At the start of every Parse every field is logged with its initial value: the value in the struct before drivers, usually zero.
  • Every driver that has changed the value of the field is logged with override. A driver that has the same value as the field already has is not logged.
  • After every reload only the fields with a new value are logged, with the driver that has set it. Unchanged fields are not logged.
[DEBUG] initial: {config: *main.Config} {field: HTTP.Port} {value: 0}
[DEBUG] override: {config: *main.Config} {driver: tag} {field: HTTP.Port} {key: initial} {value: 8080}
[DEBUG] override: {config: *main.Config} {driver: yaml} {field: HTTP.Port} {key: http.port} {value: 9000}
[DEBUG] override: {config: *main.Config} {driver: env} {field: HTTP.Port} {key: HTTP_PORT} {value: 9090}
...
[DEBUG] override: {config: *main.Config} {driver: env} {field: HTTP.Port} {key: HTTP_PORT} {value: 9091}

field is the struct path of the field in the registered config, key is the place of the value in the source of the driver:

Driver key tag name of the tag, initial yaml, json, toml, ini, properties path by the tags, http.port env name of the variable, with the prefix; HOSTS_* for the value from indexed keys flag name of the flag, -http-port consul the key, app/http/port vault path by the tags, database.password etcd the key, app/http/port

If a field has lost its value in all drivers after a reload, it gets its initial value, and it is logged without driver and key.

docs.title: Warnings of drivers
docs.text:
A driver can attach a warning to the value. The value is still used, and the warning is logged with the Warn level.

The yaml, json, toml, ini, properties, vault and format drivers warn when a parent of the field has no tag of the driver. The path to the value is built from the tags, so without the tag of the parent the value is read from another key:

type Config struct {
    HTTP struct { // no yaml tag
        Host string `yaml:"host"`
    }
}

[WARN] warning: {config: *main.Config} {driver: yaml} {field: HTTP.Host} {details: parent fields HTTP have no 'yaml' tag, the value is read from the 'host' key}

Add the tag to the parent, yaml:"http", to read the value from http.host.

docs.title: Bundled loggers
docs.text:
import "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/logger"

// prints to stdout, levels: FATAL, ERROR, WARN, INFO, DEBUG, TRACE
tinyconf.WithLogger(logger.NewFmtLogger(logger.INFO))

// wraps *slog.Logger, Go 1.21 or newer
tinyconf.WithLogger(logger.NewSlogLogger(slog.Default()))

The adapter of zap is a separate module, so zap is not a dependency of tinyconf for the applications with other loggers:

go get github.com/insei/tinyconf/logger/zaplogger

import "github.com/insei/tinyconf/logger/zaplogger"

// wraps *zap.Logger
tinyconf.WithLogger(zaplogger.New(zapLogger))

Migration

logger.NewZapLogger(l) of the previous versions is zaplogger.New(l) from the github.com/insei/tinyconf/logger/zaplogger module.

docs.title: Custom logger
docs.text:
Implement the tinyconf.Logger interface:

type Logger interface {
    Debug(msg string, fields ...Field)
    Warn(msg string, fields ...Field)
    Error(msg string, fields ...Field)
    Info(msg string, fields ...Field)
    With(fields ...Field) Logger
}

tinyconf.Field is a pair of Key and Value.

docs.title: Manager
docs.text: tinyconf.Manager holds the list of drivers and the registered configs. It is created once at the start of the application.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
config, err := tinyconf.New(
    tinyconf.WithLogger(logger.NewFmtLogger(logger.INFO)),
    tinyconf.WithDriver(tagDriver),
    tinyconf.WithDriver(yamlDriver),
    tinyconf.WithDriver(envDriver),
)
Option Description WithDriver(driver) adds the driver, can be used many times WithLogger(logger) sets the logger, see Logging

docs.title: Priority of drivers
docs.text:
Drivers are applied in the order of addition. The next driver overrides values of the previous one, so the last driver has the highest priority.

A typical order is: defaults from tags, then files, then environment variables.

A driver overrides the value only if it has a value for the field. A field that is absent in the file keeps the value from the previous driver, and a field without values in all drivers keeps the value that was in the struct before Parse.

docs.title: Register
docs.text:
c := &Config{}
err := config.Register(c)

Register takes a pointer to struct. The registered config is used by Parse and by GenDoc.

docs.title: Parse
docs.text:
err := config.Parse(context.Background(), c)

Parse fills the registered config with values from drivers. The config can be a registered one or a field of the registered config with struct type, see sub configs. tinyconf.ErrNotRegisteredConfig is returned for all other configs.

The context is used by the drivers that read their sources by the network — consul, vault, etcd and the remote documents: their requests are stopped when the context is done. A start of the application in Kubernetes is a typical case:

ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second)
defer cancel()
if err := config.Parse(ctx, c); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err) // errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) if the storage is not available in time
}

Migration

Parse(conf) of the previous versions is Parse(context.Background(), conf), and ParseContext(ctx, conf) is Parse(ctx, conf).

Every request of the drivers is limited to 30 seconds anyway. The reloads use the context of watching, so the requests are stopped when the last subscription is canceled.

docs.title: Other methods
docs.text: Method Description GenDoc(driverName) generates a template of all registered configs, see Documentation generation Sources(conf) returns which driver has set the value of every field, see Value sources tinyconf.Subscribe(ctx, m, onChange) calls onChange after the changes of the config or the sub config, see Reloading tinyconf.Current[T](m) returns the current version of the config or the sub config, see Reloading ReloadStatus() state of watching and reloading for the health checks, see Health checks

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Parse does not stop on the first error: all fields are parsed, and all errors are returned as one error. It can be checked with errors.Is and errors.As.

if err := config.Parse(context.Background(), c); err != nil {
    // env driver: field HTTP.Port: failed to parse env value from key HTTP_PORT ...
    log.Fatal(err)
}

Fields that were parsed without errors are filled even if Parse returns an error.

Missing required fields are reported in the same error and can be checked with errors.Is(err, tinyconf.ErrRequired).

Not an error

A field without a value in the driver and a field without the tag of the driver are not errors, the manager just goes to the next driver.

docs.title: Concurrency
docs.text:
All methods of the manager are safe for concurrent use: configs can be registered and parsed from several goroutines. The config struct itself is not protected, do not read it while it is being parsed by another goroutine.

Configs are documented by GenDoc and checked for sub configs in the registration order.

docs.title: Reloading
docs.text:
The manager keeps configs up to date: after every change of the config sources it parses the configs again. The application gets the current version with Current and subscribes to the changes with Subscribe.

c := &Config{}
if err := config.Register(c); err != nil {
    panic(err)
}
if err := config.Parse(context.Background(), c); err != nil {
    panic(err)
}

// a package subscribes to its part of the config
err := tinyconf.Subscribe(ctx, config, func(prev, next *HTTP) {
    if prev.Timeout != next.Timeout {
        server.SetTimeout(next.Timeout)
    }
})

// anywhere in the application
level := tinyconf.Current[Logging](config).Level

docs.title: Subscribe
docs.text:
func Subscribe[T any](ctx context.Context, m *Manager, onChange func(prev, next *T)) error
  • T is a registered config or a sub config: the type of a field of the registered config. A package subscribes to its own part and knows nothing about the whole config.
  • Subscribe does not block, the subscription is active until ctx is done.
  • onChange is called only if some fields of T are changed, with the previous and the new versions. A change of another part of the config does not call it.
  • The configs with errors are not applied: the errors are logged, the subscribers are not called and keep the last good version.

docs.title: Current
docs.text:
func Current[T any](m *Manager) *T

Current returns the current version of the config or the sub config: after the last Parse of the registered config or the last reload. It is nil before the first Parse, and for a sub config stored by pointer that is not created.

Do not change the versions

The versions from Current and onChange are shared by all readers, so they are read without locks. Never change them: copy the value if it should be changed.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Watching starts with the first subscription and stops after the context of the last one is done. One watching serves all subscribers: every driver watches its sources once for the whole application.
  • After every change the registered configs with subscribers are parsed again, from their values before drivers at the first Parse, so the result is the same as Parse would give at the start. A value removed from the file gets its default back.
  • All drivers are applied, not only the changed one: the usual priority of drivers is kept.
  • The new version replaces the current one atomically, and the subscribers of the changed parts are called.
  • The config passed to Register and Parse is never changed in the background, the application can read it as before.
  • Parse called by the application updates the current version too, but does not call the subscribers: the application knows what it does.
  • GenDoc shows the values of the current versions.

docs.title: What is watched
docs.text:
Changes are reported by drivers. The bundled yaml, json, toml, ini and properties drivers watch their files from the OS file system: the main file and the files from WithFiles. The consul driver and Consul documents are notified by Consul right after the change. The vault driver checks the versions of the secrets. The etcd driver and etcd documents watch the stream of the events of etcd.

Source Watched files from New and WithFiles yes, events of the file system and polling Consul keys and documents yes, notified by Consul Vault secrets yes, polling, every 30 seconds by default etcd keys and documents yes, notified by etcd files from WithFS, data from WithData no environment variables, flags, tags no

Files are watched by the events of the file system: inotify on Linux, kqueue on macOS and BSD, ReadDirectoryChangesW on Windows. The change is detected right after the file is written: the driver waits 100 milliseconds for the next events, so the several writes of an editor are one change.

The directories of the files are watched, not the files themselves, so everything that replaces the file works: editors, atomic renames, kubectl updates of ConfigMap volumes that replace symlinks. A file that appears or disappears is a change too.

The files are also checked by polling, every 5 seconds by default: it detects the changes when the events are not available — the limit of inotify watches is reached, the directory does not exist yet, the file system does not support events (some network file systems). The interval is set with the WithWatchInterval option of the driver:

yamlDriver, err := yaml.New("config.yaml", yaml.WithWatchInterval(time.Minute))

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Case Result the config is not registered Subscribe returns tinyconf.ErrNotRegisteredConfig, Current returns nil no driver can watch for changes Subscribe returns tinyconf.ErrNoWatchers the new config is parsed with errors the error is logged as failed to reload, the current version is kept a driver can not watch anymore, access is denied for example the error is logged, other drivers continue watching the handler panics the panic is logged as subscriber panicked, other subscribers are called

docs.title: Health checks
docs.text:
The errors of the reloads are logged, the application keeps working with the last good config. ReloadStatus shows this state for the health checks:

status := config.ReloadStatus()
Field Description Watching there are subscriptions and the sources are watched LastReload the time of the last reload LastError the error of the last reload, nil if the configs are applied LastApplied the time of the last reload without errors StoppedDrivers the drivers that can not watch anymore, with the errors: access is denied, for example

A readiness check that fails when the config is broken for a long time or a source is not watched:

func configHealthy(config *tinyconf.Manager) error {
    status := config.ReloadStatus()
    if status.LastError != nil && time.Since(status.LastApplied) > 5*time.Minute {
        return fmt.Errorf("config is not reloaded since %s: %w", status.LastApplied, status.LastError)
    }
    for driver, err := range status.StoppedDrivers {
        return fmt.Errorf("%s driver does not watch for changes: %w", driver, err)
    }
    return nil
}

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
• Handlers are called one by one in the order of subscription, from one goroutine. The next reload starts after all handlers return, so a slow handler delays the next reload.
  • Several changes that happen while the configs are being parsed are merged into one reload.
  • On the debug level only the fields with a new value are logged after a reload, with the driver that has set the value.
  • What can be applied on the fly is up to the application: a log level can be changed at any time, a listening port requires restart of the server. Compare prev and next and act on the fields that matter.

docs.title: Required fields
docs.text:
A field with the required:"true" tag should have a value. Otherwise Parse returns tinyconf.ErrRequired.

type Config struct {
    DSN      string `env:"DSN" required:"true"`
    Password string `env:"PASSWORD" yaml:"password" hidden:"true" required:"true"`
    Port     int    `env:"PORT" initial:"8080"`
}

err := config.Parse(context.Background(), c)
if errors.Is(err, tinyconf.ErrRequired) {
    // field DSN: required value is not set; field Password: required value is not set
    log.Fatal(err)
}

docs.title: What is a value
docs.text:
The field passes the check if any of these is true:

  • some driver has set its value, even if the value is zero: PORT=0 is a value;
  • the field has a non-zero value in the config that was passed to Parse.

So a required field without sources can still be filled in the code before Parse:

c := &Config{DSN: "postgres://localhost/dev"}
err := config.Parse(context.Background(), c) // DSN is not required to be in the environment

docs.title: All at once
docs.text:
Parse checks all required fields and reports all missing ones in one error, together with the errors of drivers. The application can show the full list of what should be set in one start, not one variable per attempt.

Defaults and required

A field with a default value in the tag driver always has a value, so required makes sense only for the fields without defaults: secrets, addresses of external services.

docs.title: Sub configs
docs.text: When a sub config is parsed, only its own required fields are checked.

docs.title: Value sources
docs.text:
With several drivers it is not always obvious where the final value came from. Sources returns which driver has set every field in the last Parse call.

if err := config.Parse(context.Background(), c); err != nil {
    panic(err)
}
for _, source := range config.Sources(c) {
    fmt.Printf("%s is set by %s driver from %s\n", source.Field, source.Driver, source.Source)
}

HTTP.Host is set by env driver from HTTP_HOST
HTTP.Port is set by yaml driver from http.port
Password is set by env driver from PASSWORD

docs.title: FieldSource
docs.text:
Field Description Field struct path of the field in the config, HTTP.Port for example Driver name of the driver that has set the final value Source source of the value inside the driver

Source depends on the driver:

Driver Source tag name of the tag, initial yaml, json, toml, ini, properties path by the tags, http.port env name of the variable, with the prefix; HOSTS_* for the value from indexed keys flag name of the flag, -http-port consul the key, app/http/port vault path by the tags, database.password etcd the key, app/http/port

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Sources are returned in the order of the config fields.
  • Only the last driver that has set the value is reported, the overridden ones are not.
  • Fields without values from drivers are not included: they have the value that was in the config before Parse.
  • Sources are stored per config type, pass the same pointer type that was used in Parse. For a sub config the paths are relative to it.

It is handy to log the sources once at the start of the application: the answer to "why is this value here" is in the logs. Values themselves are not included, so secrets are not leaked.

docs.title: Nested structs
docs.text:
Fields can be grouped into structs. A field with struct type is parsed by its fields, every nested field has its own tags:

type HTTP struct {
    Host string `yaml:"host" env:"HTTP_HOST" initial:"localhost"`
    Port int    `yaml:"port" env:"HTTP_PORT" initial:"8080"`
}

type Config struct {
    HTTP HTTP `yaml:"http"`
}

http:
  host: example.com
  port: 9090

For the yaml driver the tag of the struct field is a key of the nested map, so Host is read from http.host. Names of environment variables are not built from the parent names: Host is read from HTTP_HOST, as it is written in its tag.

Types that are parsed from a single value — time.Time, url.URL and types with UnmarshalText — are not nested structs, see Supported types.

docs.title: Embedded structs
docs.text:
Fields of an embedded struct without the tag are on the level of the embedding struct, like in encoding/json:

type Timeouts struct {
    Read  time.Duration `yaml:"read_timeout"`
    Write time.Duration `yaml:"write_timeout"`
}

type Config struct {
    HTTP struct {
        Timeouts
        Port int `yaml:"port"`
    } `yaml:"http"`
}

http:
  port: 9090
  read_timeout: 5s
  write_timeout: 10s
  • The yaml, json, toml, ini, properties, consul, vault and etcd drivers read Read from http.read_timeout, the embedded struct adds no level. yaml:",inline" works the same way.
  • With the name in the tag, Timeouts `yaml:"timeouts"`, the embedded struct is a usual nested struct: http.timeouts.read_timeout.
  • An embedded struct without the tag is expected, the manager does not warn about it.
  • Auto keys and indexed keys of the env driver skip the name of the embedded struct too: HTTP.Timeouts.Read is HTTP_READ with auto keys, and SERVERS_0_READ for the struct in the slice.

docs.title: Structs stored by pointer
docs.text:
A struct stored by pointer is parsed the same way, by its fields:

type TLS struct {
    Cert string `yaml:"cert" env:"TLS_CERT"`
    Key  string `yaml:"key" env:"TLS_KEY"`
}

type Config struct {
    TLS *TLS `yaml:"tls"`
}

The pointer makes the section optional:

  • the struct is created when the first value for its fields is found in any driver;
  • without values the pointer is not changed, so it stays nil;
  • an existing struct is filled in place, it is not replaced with a new one.
if err := config.Parse(context.Background(), c); err != nil {
    panic(err)
}
if c.TLS != nil {
    // TLS_CERT, TLS_KEY or the tls section of the file is set
}

Required fields inside such struct are checked even if the pointer is nil: a required field makes the whole section mandatory.

Parsed as a single value

Pointers to pointers (**Struct) and recursive types (Next *Node inside Node) are not parsed by fields. They are single values: JSON in string values, a nested map in files.

docs.title: Sub configs
docs.text:
A part of the registered config can be parsed separately, by the type of the field. It allows a package to get its own config without knowing about the whole one:

c := &Config{}
if err := config.Register(c); err != nil {
    panic(err)
}

// HTTP is a type of the field in the registered Config
http := &HTTP{}
if err := config.Parse(context.Background(), http); err != nil {
    panic(err)
}

The type can be a type of the struct stored by value or by pointer. Only the fields of the sub config are parsed, with the same tags and keys as in the whole config: http.host in the file, HTTP_HOST in the environment.

If several registered configs have a field with this type, the configs are checked in the registration order and the first found field is used.

docs.title: Struct tags
docs.text:
Everything about a field is described by its struct tags: where the value comes from, how it is documented and how it is parsed.

type Config struct {
    Token string   `yaml:"token" env:"TOKEN" initial:"dev" doc:"API token" hidden:"true"`
    Hosts []string `yaml:"hosts" env:"HOSTS" separator:";"`
}

docs.title: Driver tags
docs.text:
Every driver reads its own tag, the value of the tag is the name of the value in the source of the driver.

Driver Tag Value tag any, set in tag.New the default value itself yaml yaml key in the file json json key in the file toml toml key in the file env env name of the environment variable flag flag name of the command line flag

A field without the tag of the driver is skipped by this driver.

docs.title: Common tags
docs.text:
Tag Description doc:"text" description of the field for GenDoc merge:"true" slices and maps from several drivers are merged instead of replaced, see Several drivers hidden:"true" the value is masked in logs and is not shown in GenDoc, use it for secrets; see also the Secret type required:"true" Parse returns an error if the field has no value, see Required fields separator:";" separator of slice, array and map items in string values, , by default kvseparator:"=" separator of map key and value in string values, : by default

See Supported types for the syntax of string values.

docs.title: Supported types
docs.text:
All drivers support the same set of types. It is checked by the conformance tests in drivers/conformance_test.go: every type is parsed by every driver, and the results should be equal.

Drivers get values in two forms:

  • string values — environment variables, command line flags and struct tags;
  • native values — YAML, JSON and TOML, where lists and maps are a part of the format.
Types String value Native value string, bool, integers, floats and named types based on them value scalar time.Duration 1m30s 1m30s time.Time 2024-01-02T03:04:05Z, 2024-01-02 03:04:05, 2024-01-02 the same or yaml timestamp url.URL, []byte, any encoding.TextUnmarshaler (net.IP, uuid.UUID, ...) value scalar []T, [N]T a,b,c list or string map[K]V a:1,b:2 map or string []Struct, map[K]Struct, nested slices and maps JSON: [{"host":"a","port":1}] native pointers to all types above the same the same Struct, *Struct parsed by fields parsed by fields

docs.title: Slices and arrays
docs.text:
type Config struct {
    Hosts []string `env:"HOSTS" yaml:"hosts"`
    Ports [2]int   `env:"PORTS" yaml:"ports"`
}
envyaml 
HOSTS=a.example.com,b.example.com
PORTS=80,443

hosts: [a.example.com, b.example.com]
ports:
  - 80
  - 443

Items that contain the separator can be quoted with double or single quotes: "a,b",c is two items. The separator can be changed with the separator tag. The number of items for an array should be equal to its length.

docs.title: Maps
docs.text:
type Config struct {
    Labels map[string]string `env:"LABELS" yaml:"labels"`
    Limits map[string]int    `env:"LIMITS" yaml:"limits" separator:";" kvseparator:"="`
}
envyaml 
LABELS=env:prod,team:core
LIMITS=cpu=2;memory=512

labels:
  env: prod
  team: core
limits: {cpu: 2, memory: 512}

docs.title: Structs in slices and maps
docs.text:
Nested values are set as JSON in string values and as is in YAML, JSON and TOML files:

type Server struct {
    Host string `json:"host" yaml:"host"`
    Port int    `json:"port" yaml:"port"`
}

type Config struct {
    Servers []Server `env:"SERVERS" yaml:"servers"`
}
envyaml 
SERVERS='[{"host":"a","port":1},{"host":"b","port":2}]'

servers:
  - host: a
    port: 1
  - host: b
    port: 2

String values of slices, arrays, maps and structs are parsed as JSON if they start with [ or {. Keys of such structs are taken from the json tag for string values and JSON files, from the yaml tag for YAML files and from the toml tag for TOML files, the field name is used if the tag is not set (case-insensitive).

Fields with struct type

A field with struct type, stored by value or by pointer, is not a single value: it is parsed by its fields, and every field has its own tags. See Nested structs and sub configs.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
tinyconf.Secret is a string that is not printed. hidden:"true" masks the value in the logs of tinyconf, but the application can print or log the whole config itself; the Secret type masks the value there too:

type Config struct {
    Database struct {
        User     string          `env:"DB_USER"`
        Password tinyconf.Secret `env:"DB_PASSWORD"`
    }
}

log.Printf("config: %+v", conf)            // {Database:{User:app Password:******}}
db.Connect(conf.Database.User, conf.Database.Password.Value())
  • String, GoString and MarshalText return ****** for a not empty value, so fmt, encoding/json, yaml, zap and slog print the mask. The length of the value is not shown; an empty value is shown as empty, so it is visible that the secret is not set.
  • The value is parsed like a usual string by all drivers, slices and pointers of secrets work too.
  • Value() or string(secret) returns the value.
  • GenDoc shows ****** as the value of the field.

docs.title: Several drivers
docs.text:
If the value of a slice or map is provided by several drivers, the last driver replaces the whole value. With the merge:"true" tag the values are merged:

type Config struct {
    Hosts  []string          `initial:"default" yaml:"hosts" env:"HOSTS" merge:"true"`
    Labels map[string]string `initial:"team:core" yaml:"labels" env:"LABELS" merge:"true"`
}

# config.yaml: hosts: [from-file], labels: {env: dev}
HOSTS=from-env LABELS=env:prod
# Hosts:  [default from-file from-env]
# Labels: map[env:prod team:core]
  • Slices are appended in the order of the drivers, pointers to slices too.
  • Maps get the keys of the next drivers, the same key is overridden by the next driver.
  • The values of the drivers in one Parse call are merged: the first driver with the value replaces the value of the struct, so the next Parse does not duplicate the items.
  • Arrays, []byte and other types are replaced.
  • Sources reports the last driver, the log has every step.
